column2: Thus making the linga joined with placements and the rest, one incurs no fault. Having then made the pedestal-binding, with the mark of the part of the mark,
having brought the Gauri mantra to dissolution one should place the pedestal by creation; having filled, the perfection of the sides, a plaster of sand and adamant;
then the teacher with the form-bearers, above the pot, having established peace with other pots likewise with the five nectars and the rest,
having anointed with sandal and the rest and worshipped the lord of the world, one should touch both with the linga-mudra with the Uma-Mahesha mantras.
Then having made the placing of the three principles preceded by the six worships, the form, and of the lords' limbs and Brahmas,
the knower, having removed on the linga, on the seat of Kriya, should then bathe; having anointed with scents and fumigated, he should place Shiva as pervading.
With garlands, incense, lamps, food and fruits with the heart-mantra, having offered as able, having rinsed, the great Lord —
having given arghya and done repetition, having offered in the boon-giving hand: "As long as moon, sun and stars, by the mantra, with the Shaiva form-lords,
of your own will, Lord, you must stay here in this temple." Having bowed, going outside, with the heart-mantra or with Om,
having set up the bull afterward one should make the offering as before. To remove faults of deficiency and the rest, then with Mrityunjaya a hundred,
with Shiva with Shiva, offering also with pudding for peace: "Whatever was done by knowledge or ignorance, complete that, great Lord."
Gold, cattle, land and the like, for songs, instruments and the like, to Ambikesha one should devoutly offer all according to ability.
Afterward one should make gifts and a great festival for four days. For three days the mantra-master should offer at the three twilights with the form-lords.
On the fourth day one should offer the full oblation and the porridge with the many-formed, purified by the Sampata oblation in all pits.
For four days, that remnant after it; having removed the remnant and bathed, one should worship.
Worship in ordinary lingas is to be done with common atoms. Leaving the linga's consciousness, one should do the dismissal of the Sthanu.
In extraordinary lingas, the dismissal is with "Forgive." Invocation, manifestation, emission, the state of power:
at the end of installation sometimes the sevenfold oblation beginning with "steady" is told: Steady, and the immeasurable, and of beginningless awareness likewise,
eternal, all-going, imperishable, and seen — these qualities of the Great Lord are declared for his presence.
Om, homage to Shiva, be steady is the order of oblations. Having thus accomplished this and made it like Shiva's pot,
two pots; from among them with the water of one pot having bathed Bhava, and the second one should hold for the sacrificer's bath.
Having given the offering and rinsed, one should go outside at Shiva's command. Outside the platform, in the northeast, for Chanda in a temple,
in a seat arranged on a good pedestal of the measure of the sanctum; having done placement, oblation and the rest as before, preceded by meditation,
having duly established there one should worship with Brahma-limbs. The limbs as before, and the worship of Brahmani;

thus: "To Sadyojata, Om Hrum phat, homage; Om Vim, to Vamadeva, Hrum phat, homage; Om Bum, to Aghora, Hrum phat, homage; Om, to Tatpurusha, vaum to Ishana, Hrum phat." Having offered repetition, satisfied and informed with bowing: "As long as the god is present, so long be present;
whatever excess or deficiency was done by me through ignorance, by your grace, Chandesha, complete all that."
In a Bana linga, in one risen from a river, a Siddha linga, a self-born one, and in all images Chanda is not the one in authority.
Even in a rite of the platform-lord endowed with the notion of non-duality, having worshipped Chanda, the sacrificer with his wife and son,
the bather should not himself bathe in the pot established earlier; and the sacrificer too, having worshipped the establisher like Mahesha,
should give without stinginess land, gold and the like as fee; afterward the embodied one by rule, the reciters, Brahmins likewise,
having worshipped the astrologer and the sculptor, should feed the poor, helpless and others: "Whatever in this face-to-face state has troubled you, Lord, by me,
forgive all that, Lord, ocean of compassion for me." To the sacrificer who has thus petitioned, the good teacher
should present with his own hand the virtue of the installation, shining like stars, with kusha, flowers and rice.
Then, having bowed to the Supreme Lord with the Pashupata, and with offerings having made the beings present, one should instruct:
You must stay as long as Hara is present. The teacher should take the sacrificial hall with cloths and the rest,
the sculptor all the implements and likewise the bathing pavilion. Other gods and the rest are to be installed with mantras arising from the scriptures,
or by difference of the first letter, contemplated as pervaded by the good principles. The Sadhyas and chief gods, rivers and herbs,
field-guardians, Kinnaras and others rest on the earth-principle. The bath sometimes in the water of Sarasvati, Lakshmi and the rivers;
the place where the lords of worlds are established; the three principles up to the egg's growth and primal nature are Brahma's station;
from the subtle elements up to primal nature is this triad, Hari's station; of Nateshvara, hosts, mothers, Yakshesha and the Shara-born,
the egg-born up to pure knowledge is also the station of Ganapati; from the Maya-portion up to the power of the region, Shiva's... of the Shiva-born radiances
the station up to Ishvara is declared in manifest worships. What is declared beginning with Kurma, and the five jewels and the rest,
one should throw into the pedestal pit, except the five Brahma stones. In a pit divided by six, leaving the feeling and the back,
installation in the fifth part, or if divided by eight, installation in the seventh part is pleasing for images.
Purification by contemplations in the installation of plaster and painted images; bathing and the rest mental there; placing of stone, jewels and the rest;
opening the eyes, mantra, desired seat and the rest to be arranged; worship with flowers without water, so that the picture is not spoiled.
The rule for movable lingas is now stated: when divided by five or by three, one should do separately;
the portion share by three parts or by two parts; in one's own pedestals likewise, in lingas, by difference of principles.
Preparation with the creation-mantra by rule in crystal and the rest; moreover non-offering of Brahma stone, jewels and the like,
and the joining of the pedestal one should arrange in mind. In a self-born or Bana linga and the like there is no rule for consecration.
One should have bathing with Samhita mantras, placement and oblation done; the installation of river and ocean-born ones is held as before.
A worldly clay linga, or one of flour and the like by carving, having made, one should worship pure by the rule of gazing and the rest;
then having taken the mantras and made the Self present, one should cast the linga into its water; in a year it gives desires.
The installation of Vishnu and others one should do with separate mantras.
Rochana, ruk, vacha, durva, and a bundle below the temple; having made it in nature, tied to an udumbara for protection with Om;
one should place the door slightly leaning northward; placing the Self-principle below and the knowledge-principle on the door-posts;
Shiva in space, the pervading all-auspicious; then one should place Maheshanatha with the root-mantra.
Those dependent on the door and the couch and the like, with proper own names, one should offer a hundred or half, or double according to ability;
for removing faults of deficiency and the rest one should offer a hundred with the weapon-mantra; having offered the directional offering as before one should give the fee and the rest.
Having taken from the twelve-end, like a shining spark of fire, one should cast it in the pot's womb, the conveyor of the placed tantra;
the body, the awakener of its qualities, the digits and the rest; at peace, Vagishvara; one should place that group there.
Ten channels, ten breaths and thirteen senses, having joined their lords by their own names beginning with Om,
as regulators of the Maya-space by being cause of their own effects, the knowledge-lords, the impellers, Shambhu and the all-pervading, with good coverings,
having placed the limbs one should enclose with the restraining mudra. Or a person arisen from gold and the like, following the person,
then prepared as before with the five cow-products and astringents; having placed the pot on the couch, having meditated on Rudra, lord of Uma,
one should place in it by the Shiva-mantra as pervading. For presence, the oblation, sprinkling, touching, repetition,
the awakening of presence — all by the division of three portions; having thus done, at the end of nature one should place him in the pot.
On the staff the principle of meaning and the second the knowledge-principle; the faces Sadyojata and the rest; the Shiva-principle again on the banner;
and the partless Shiva there; having placed the limbs one should worship. On the crest then the mantra, in presence with Samhita atoms,
one should offer for each portion on the banner with those ending in phat. And whatever banner-preparation is done otherwise anywhere,
in the rite of weapon worship all that is shown. In the place where the temple is built, adorned with garlands, cloths and the rest,
having placed on the thigh-altar and above it the three principles and the rest, having done oblation and so on, having worshipped Shiva as before,
having meditated on the all-principle form, one should place Shiva as pervading; having meditated Ananta and Kalarudra at the lotus feet,
Kushmanda and Hataka on the pedestal with the underworlds and hells, surrounded by worlds, guardians of the world, hundred Rudras and the rest,
having meditated this egg of Brahma, one should imagine the lower body; joined with water, fire, air, space — the five-eight;
called the all-covering, joined with the growth-wombs and wolves; joined with the yoga-eight, the rule of destruction, the three qualities;
one should contemplate the Person on the cloth, the lion and the left; on the altar-spire the knowledge-four and the rest;
in the throat Maya with Rudras; and knowledges in the spotless essence; in the pot Ishvara, bindu, with the lord of knowledge;
know the matted crest, the trident, half-moon form; and three powers there; having contemplated nada on the staff;
on the banner the coiled power — thus one should contemplate in the abode; or having joined the linga with the pedestal on the ground.
